competencyTargets.label: Sample and assess vegetation using standardized field protocols
Detect and record wildlife by direct observation, sign and standardized surveys
Measure water quality and survey aquatic communities in the field
Identify organisms from field characters, specimens, images and recordings
Record field observations with protocol fidelity and data integrity
Manage field sample custody and field quality control
Navigate and travel safely in remote terrain with and without digital aids
Manage risk in uncontrolled field environments
Ground-truth remote-sensed, modelled and AI-generated outputs in the field
Describe, test and sample soils in the field
Provide first aid and emergency medical care in remote field settings
Collect trace-level and genetic environmental samples without contamination
Apply field biosecurity and decontamination protocols
Operate small boats and work safely on water in aquatic, coastal and marine field settings
Operate and supervise uncrewed and automated field systems
Deploy, maintain and verify field sensor networks
Lead field crews and transfer field judgment to novices
Read site history and reference conditions from landscape evidence
Drive and operate field vehicles safely on unpaved roads and off road
Apply safety practices and stop-work authority across field, facility and incident settings
Interpret and question environmental data products in everyday work
Use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work
Validate AI-generated work products before professional use
Record provenance and AI involvement in work products

topTasks.statement: Establish vegetation monitoring plots to protocol and record species composition, cover and density within the program's measurement-quality objectives
Identify plants on sample plots to the protocol's required taxonomic level, collecting labelled vouchers for any plant not identified with certainty
Adapt the vegetation sampling layout when burned, flooded or grazed site conditions depart from protocol assumptions, recording the deviation for comparability
Conduct point-count, transect or call-playback wildlife surveys to protocol, recording detections, distance bands and survey conditions
Identify wildlife sign such as tracks, scat, nests and feeding remains to species or group, recording a confidence level for each record
Deploy camera traps and acoustic recorders at survey stations to the protocol's height, orientation and settings, recording station metadata
Measure temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen, conductivity and turbidity in place with field meters calibrated before use and checked afterward
Collect grab water samples at locations and depths that represent the condition of interest, recording flow and site conditions at collection
Collect benthic macroinvertebrate, algae or fish community samples from a stream reach following the program's habitat-allocation protocol
Describe a soil profile's horizons, colour, texture, structure and coarse fragments in standard terminology on the program's description form
Collect soil samples at specified depths and locations for laboratory analysis of texture, nutrients, carbon or contaminants
Identify regional plants and animals to species with dichotomous keys and diagnostic features, collecting evidence for any record not identified with certainty
